title: Merchant entry heuristics and voice lab
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight playbook + quick audit rubric for merchant/partner marketplace entries. Goal is to speed review cycles for listing teams and provide ready-to-copy tile/snippet variants that match our tone while calling out clear risk gates. Use this as the intake reviewer shorthand during fast cycles and hand off to legal/secure only for flagged cases.

Quick notes to reviewers (TL;DR):
- Fast accept if: minimal external integration, no exec access, no customer data ingestion, clear EULA, no restricted vertical claims.
- Escalate if: requests for billing integration, SSO/KMS, data residency claims, or health/financial vertical language.
- Copy priority: truth-first -> benefit -> quick CTA. Keep technical claims measurable and avoid superlatives unless substantiated.

Acceptance heuristics (short rubric for a 3–5 minute triage):
1) Functional compatibility (pass/fail)
   - Does the tile describe what the product actually does? (pass = yes explicit)
   - Is there any implied capability we know isn’t supported by Redwood? (fail if yes)
2) Data & privacy risk (low/medium/high)
   - Does merchant claim they store/process customer PII or PHI? (medium/high)
   - Any mention of residency requirements or cross-border processing? (escalate)
3) Technical gate (ok/needs follow-up)
   - Does offering require Private/VPC or KMS/HSM? (needs follow-up)
   - Any custom model binaries or customer-managed infra? (needs SRE/Private-eng review)
4) Billing / entitlement (ok/needs billing flow design)
   - Is merchant using our metered tokens or their own billing? If combining, route to billing ops.
5) Legal/compliance triggers (boolean)
   - Health, Finance, or Law-specific advice implied? If yes, legal review required.

Fast-accept checklist (when all apply -> green):
- Tile copy limited to product features and platform integration (no regulated claims)
- No custom infra or tenant isolation needed
- No ingestion of PHI/PII or controlled datasets
- Pricing model uses our standard metered SKU or is self-contained trial
- Assets provided: hero image (1024x576), short tile (120 chars), long description (500–700 chars), 3 bullet benefits

Copy voice & micro-guidelines (engineer-friendly, direct, benefits-first):
- Tone: pragmatic, specific, slightly technical but accessible. Avoid marketing superlatives ("industry-leading") unless we have bench data.
- Lead with value: "Reduce inference latency for real-time chat by 40%" is better than "Fast".
- Use nouns not adjectives for features: "dedicated GPU pools" vs "fast GPUs".
- Include a single action line: "Start a free trial" or "Contact sales for Dedicated".

Tile & snippet variants (ready to copy into marketplace fields):
- Tile (short, 100–130 chars):
  "Ship LLM features at predictable cost—hosted API, dedicated instances, and private deployments with observability and rollouts."

- Short summary (200–300 chars):
  "Redwood Inference gives engineering teams a unified runtime for production LLM serving: hosted API for quick demos, reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput, and private deployments for regulated workloads. Built-in tracing, cost telemetry, and rollout controls."

- Long description (approx 520 chars):
  "Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Ship chat, generation, and embeddings with production SLOs—automatic batching, caching, model variant routing, and cost-aware controls. Teams can pin model versions, run canary rollouts, and get token- and route-level visibility without building a custom serving stack."

- Three benefit bullets (concise):
  1) Predictable performance: reserved GPU pools and autoscale policies for steady latency and throughput.
  2) Cost controls: batching, quantization suggestions, and token-level visibility to reduce unit economics.
  3) Enterprise-ready: private deployments, KMS integrations, and audit logs for regulated customers.

Micro-variants for A/B tests (keep naturally switching 1–2 words):
- Variant A CTA: "Start free trial"
- Variant B CTA: "Try hosted API"
- Variant A lead: "Ship LLM features at predictable cost"
- Variant B lead: "Deploy production-grade LLM inference, fast"

Operational gate matrix (who to loop in based on triage):
- Legal: any PHI/PII claims, health/finance verticals, or partnership revenue share requests
- Billing: custom entitlement routes, combined billing models, or marketplace revenue split changes
- SRE / Private-eng: requests for on-prem bundles, tenant isolation, KMS/HSM, or bespoke autoscale
- Security: any SSO/SCIM requests or requests to accept third-party code/artifacts

Common risk scenarios and suggested mitigations:
1) Merchant claims "HIPAA-ready" but lacks BAAs or audit docs -> Mitigation: require legal sign-off and a technical checklist for PHI handling; block listing until docs provided.
2) Listing implies "zero-shot enterprise accuracy" or other unverifiable benchmark -> Mitigation: ask for benchmark methodology or remove superlative language; replace with measured statement like "evaluated on X dataset, Y score".
3) Seller wants combined billing (their SaaS + Redwood tokens) with a split -> Mitigation: route to billing ops to define flow and ensure telemetry mapping; do not publish until clear entitlements defined.
4) Partner uploads model binaries or runtime containers -> Mitigation: require security scan, provenance proof, and Private-eng review for signing and deployment model.

Reviewer quick script (copy-paste for triage Slack message):
"Quick triage for listing X: Functional OK, Data risk: LOW, Billing: needs-billing-op, Tech gate: needs-private-eng (KMS). Recommend hold for billing + private-eng review. Flagged copy for 'HIPAA-ready' claim — request substantiation."

Checklist for copy-edit pass (editor + reviewer):
- Remove unsubstantiated superlatives
- Replace vague claims with measurable or linkable proof
- Confirm CTA maps to correct landing page/trial flow
- Ensure hero image is company-branded and not trademark-violating
- Confirm contact/support email is a monitored alias

Examples of harmful phrases to flag (auto-scan candidates):
- "Best-in-class", "industry-leading", "HIPAA-ready" without docs, "bank-grade" without certifications, "guaranteed accuracy"

Workflows & tooling recommendations (ops notes):
- Add a triage label "fast-audit" for listings that meet Fast-accept checklist to skip full reviews.
- Provide an internal Confluence template that auto-populates required assets and checkboxes to shorten back-and-forth. (see linked artifact)
- Keep a small repo of approved hero image assets and templated tile copy for 1-click insertion.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we quietly standardize CTAs to two canonical phrases to simplify analytics? ("Start free trial" vs "Try hosted API")
- Can we get a simple legal decision tree for PHI/PII claims to reduce cycles?
- Need a short internal example pack (3 approved tiles + assets) to speed review for common partner types (ISV, connector, analytics).

Notes to self / meeting scraps:
- Miguel: prototype template for image naming conventions (ASAP)
- Liam: work with billing ops to document token mapping for combined-billing flows
- Dana: draft a 1-page legal decision tree for health/finance claims
